en.title: Minimalist Tattoo Ideas: Simple Designs with Personal Meaning
en.description: Explore minimalist tattoo ideas with three editable prompts, practical composition tips and a photo-preview checklist before discussing a design with your artist.
en.intro: A minimalist tattoo starts with a clear idea and a small number of marks. A single stem, an open circle or a short continuous line can carry a personal story without a busy composition. Use these starting points to explore a custom concept, then compare how it reads on your own photo.

sections.title: Choose one subject before choosing a style
sections.body: Start with something specific: a flower you grow, a coastline you remember or a shape associated with an important moment. Describe that subject first, followed by the line style and amount of detail. “Minimal design tattoo” is a useful search phrase, but a prompt needs more direction. A single olive branch with five leaves tells the image model more than “a beautiful meaningful tattoo.” Avoid combining several unrelated symbols until the main idea works on its own.

sections.title: Small does not have to mean intricate
sections.body: For a small concept, compare a sparse silhouette with a version that has a few internal details. Check both at the size you expect to wear, rather than judging only a large image on a screen. Very small lettering or tightly packed lines may look convincing in an AI image without making a practical tattoo. Your artist can advise on line spacing, size and how the design might change over time; a preview cannot predict those outcomes.

sections.title: Preview the composition on a clear body photo
sections.body: Use an evenly lit photo with the intended area visible. The Preview studio separates design from try-on: upload or generate a design, then move, resize and rotate it freely. Each try-on produces one image. Save and reuse designs free, adjusting placement before another try-on. A preview cannot measure exact physical size or replace an artist’s review.

sections.title: Keep a reference for the artist conversation
sections.body: Save the design you like and note what you would change: fewer leaves, more empty space, a shorter stem or a different direction. Treat the image as a conversation starter. The tattoo artist should redraw or adapt it for your anatomy and technique. Check the original photo against the preview as well: AI can change skin, pose, proportions or background details along with the tattoo.

prompts.title: A botanical line
prompts.text: A minimalist black-ink olive branch tattoo, one slender curved stem with five clearly separated leaves, fine clean outlines, generous negative space, no lettering, isolated on a white background.
prompts.note: Swap olive for a plant that has a personal connection. Compare a straight stem with a curved one.

prompts.title: A remembered landscape
prompts.text: A simple minimalist mountain tattoo, one continuous black line forming two uneven peaks and a small open sun, horizontal composition, no shading, no text, isolated on white.
prompts.note: Name a landscape feature you remember instead of adding several generic travel symbols.

prompts.title: An open geometric mark
prompts.text: A minimalist geometric tattoo with one incomplete circle and a short offset vertical line, balanced negative space, crisp black ink, no decorative dots or lettering, isolated on white.
prompts.note: A shape has no guaranteed universal meaning. Decide what it represents to you before adding a caption.

en.title: Geometric Tattoo Ideas: Wolf Designs, Shapes and Prompt Examples
en.description: Plan a geometric tattoo with editable wolf and shape prompts. See a real saved try-on example, compare symmetry and detail, and prepare a reference for your tattoo artist.
en.intro: Geometric tattoo designs use repeated shapes, angular outlines or structured spacing to build an image. They can be entirely abstract or use geometry to describe a familiar subject, such as a wolf. The choice is less about adding more triangles and more about choosing a shape language that stays readable.

sections.title: Decide how much geometry the subject needs
sections.body: Try describing the same subject in two ways: an angular silhouette with very little interior detail, and a more detailed head divided into faceted shapes. The first version emphasizes the outline; the second emphasizes the face and pattern. For a wolf, specify whether you want a front-facing symmetrical head or a side profile. Mixing both instructions often gives the model conflicting directions.

sections.title: Use the saved example as a workflow reference
sections.body: The homepage Gundam example follows a saved photo, an uploaded design and a preset biceps placement through to one real saved result, free to explore. The Preview studio uses free placement and single-image try-ons: reuse a design and adjust its position before submitting each comparison. Compare outline, detail and negative space at different sizes and locations.

sections.title: Compare detail at the intended viewing size
sections.body: Zoom out as well as in. A dense geometric pattern may look impressive enlarged but become visually crowded when reduced. Compare the spacing between shapes, the weight of the outer outline and the amount of uninked space around the face. If the eyes or central shapes seem uneven, simplify the prompt and generate another concept rather than assuming an artist can use the image unchanged.

sections.title: Separate a visual concept from a tattoo stencil
sections.body: An AI geometric tattoo image is a design reference, not a verified stencil. It may contain broken lines, inconsistent symmetry or details that do not wrap naturally around a limb. Ask an artist to adapt the layout and check the linework. A photo preview is also an approximation: compare it with the original to identify changes to body shape or lighting before using it to make a placement decision.

prompts.title: Black-and-grey geometric wolf
prompts.text: A front-facing geometric wolf head tattoo, symmetrical angular facets, black and grey shading, clear eyes and muzzle, fine outlines with restrained dotwork, vertical composition, no text, isolated on white.
prompts.note: This is a prompt starting point inspired by the homepage example, not a promise to reproduce that exact design.

prompts.title: Simple geometric shapes
prompts.text: A small geometric tattoo made of two offset open triangles and a single circle, clean black outlines, consistent line weight, generous empty space, no shading or lettering, isolated on white.
prompts.note: Use a small number of shapes first. Add one detail at a time if the design feels too sparse.

prompts.title: An abstract animal profile
prompts.text: A geometric fox side-profile tattoo built from a few large angular shapes, clear pointed ears and a long muzzle, black linework with limited grey shading, no border, no text, white background.
prompts.note: Changing the animal also changes the silhouette. Keep the profile instruction consistent.

en.title: First Tattoo Ideas: From a Personal Concept to a Photo Preview
en.description: Find first tattoo ideas with a clear brief, three adaptable prompts and a practical photo-preview checklist to help you discuss design and placement with an artist.
en.intro: Choosing a first tattoo is easier when you separate the decisions: what the image represents, how much detail you want, where you are considering wearing it and what you still need to ask an artist. A photo preview helps you compare visual options without making those decisions for you.

sections.title: Write a brief before collecting more ideas
sections.body: Choose one subject and write one sentence explaining why you like it. Then add a visual preference: outlined or shaded, compact or elongated, quiet or bold. You do not need to give every tattoo a deep meaning; liking the image is also a valid starting point. What matters is being specific enough to compare alternatives. Save the brief alongside the images so that later changes still connect to your original idea.

sections.title: Compare a few distinct directions
sections.body: Instead of generating many nearly identical versions, try a simple line drawing, a bolder silhouette and a more detailed interpretation of the same subject. Compare what each version emphasizes. The prompt examples below use a botanical motif, a landscape and a geometric animal so you can test different visual directions. Use your own subject rather than treating a search result as a design you must copy.

sections.title: Think about placement in your everyday context
sections.body: Consider visibility in everyday clothing and how the design relates to the body area. Use an evenly lit photo with the intended area visible. In the Preview studio, move, resize and rotate a design, then generate one try-on image. Reuse that design to compare another position. A photo cannot measure pain, predict healing or guarantee a real-world result.

sections.title: Use AI previews to prepare questions
sections.body: Make a short list for your tattoo artist: Could this work at the size I want? Which details need simplifying? Would the outline need to change for this placement? Share both the standalone design and the body preview where available. Your artist can assess technique and adapt the concept; an AI image should not replace that discussion. If the AI changes your body shape, skin or surroundings, judge the design separately from those changes.

sections.title: Know what the free example and credits provide
sections.body: Explore the saved homepage example free. Preview uses separate test credits, never real account balances: one 1K design costs 1 credit; a single 1K, 2K or 4K try-on costs 1, 2 or 3 credits. Uploading, saving, reusing and positioning are free. AI requests still incur KIE test costs and require explicit consent. Designs and history stay in this browser. The live signup offer of 3 credits after email verification keeps its existing terms; Preview offers no real purchases.

prompts.title: One meaningful botanical subject
prompts.text: A small black-ink tattoo of a single rosemary sprig, clean outline, a few clearly separated leaves, no heavy shading, simple vertical composition, no text, isolated on white.
prompts.note: Replace rosemary with a plant you actually want to wear; keep the first version focused on one stem.

prompts.title: A quiet landscape
prompts.text: A simple tattoo concept of a low sun above one curved ocean wave, black linework, compact balanced composition, open negative space, no lettering or frame, white background.
prompts.note: Ask for a second version with a bolder outline so you can compare the visual weight.

prompts.title: A structured animal design
prompts.text: A geometric bird tattoo with open wings, a few large angular shapes, recognizable silhouette, black outlines with very limited grey shading, no text, isolated on a white background.
prompts.note: If the anatomy looks inconsistent, simplify the concept and review the final reference with an artist.

zh.title: 极简纹身灵感：把个人想法变成清晰的设计
zh.description: 从植物、线条和几何符号探索极简纹身，参考可修改的英文提示词，学习如何比较照片效果并准备与纹身师沟通的设计参考。
zh.intro: 极简纹身的重点，是用少量线条表达清楚的想法。可以从一段记忆、一种植物或一个形状开始，再比较构图与细节，而不是把许多象征元素都放进同一张设计。

sections.title: 先选主题，再确定风格
sections.body: 把“想要一个有意义的纹身”写得更具体：例如一枝五片叶子的橄榄枝，或记忆里两座高低不同的山峰。先说明主体，再说明线条、阴影和留白。第一次尝试可以只保留一个主题，等主体清晰后再加入其他元素。

sections.title: 小图案也需要足够的空间
sections.body: 同时比较简洁轮廓与少量内部细节两个版本。不要只看放大的屏幕图，要缩小到接近希望呈现的视觉大小。非常细小的文字、密集线条可能在 AI 图像中好看，但不能据此判断实际可纹性或长期效果，需要纹身师评估尺寸和间距。

sections.title: 用清晰的身体照片比较构图
sections.body: 使用光线均匀、目标部位清晰可见的照片。Preview 工作室将设计与试戴分开：先上传或生成图案，再自由移动、缩放和旋转，每次试戴生成一张图片。可以免费保存和复用设计，调整位置后再次试戴。预览不是精确尺寸测量工具，也不能替代纹身师确认。

sections.title: 记录你真正想修改的部分
sections.body: 保存喜欢的图案，并写下想减少的叶片、希望加大的留白或想改变的方向。把它作为和纹身师讨论的参考。对照原照片检查皮肤、姿势、比例和背景，因为 AI 也可能改动纹身以外的画面。

prompts.title: 植物细线
prompts.text: A minimalist black-ink olive branch tattoo, one slender curved stem with five clearly separated leaves, fine clean outlines, generous negative space, no lettering, isolated on a white background.
prompts.note: 把橄榄换成与你有联系的植物，比较直线与弧线的构图。

prompts.title: 记忆里的山峰
prompts.text: A simple minimalist mountain tattoo, one continuous black line forming two uneven peaks and a small open sun, horizontal composition, no shading, no text, isolated on white.
prompts.note: 用真实记忆里的地貌替换泛泛的旅行符号。

prompts.title: 开放的几何符号
prompts.text: A minimalist geometric tattoo with one incomplete circle and a short offset vertical line, balanced negative space, crisp black ink, no decorative dots or lettering, isolated on white.
prompts.note: 形状没有保证通用的含义，可以先想清楚它对你个人的意义。

zh.title: 几何纹身设计：狼头、抽象形状与提示词示例
zh.description: 用几何狼头与简洁形状探索纹身设计，参考可修改提示词，查看网站真实案例，比较对称性、留白与身体照片上的效果。
zh.intro: 几何纹身可以用重复形状、棱角轮廓和有规律的间距组织画面。它既能表现狼头等具体主体，也可以完全抽象。关键是选择清楚的视觉语言，而不是不断增加三角形。

sections.title: 先决定主体与几何的关系
sections.body: 同一只狼可以用简洁的棱角轮廓表现，也可以用多个切面构成立体的脸部。前者重视外形，后者重视图案与面部细节。提示词应明确正面、对称狼头或侧面轮廓，避免把矛盾的角度要求写在一起。

sections.title: 观察首页真实保存的试戴案例
sections.body: 首页高达案例展示从原图、上传图案、固定肱二头肌位置到一张已保存试戴结果的过程，浏览免费。Preview 工作室采用自由定位、单张试戴：复用设计并调整位置后，分别提交想比较的效果。观察不同大小与位置的轮廓、细节和留白。

sections.title: 放大与缩小都要看
sections.body: 密集的几何图案在大图中可能很漂亮，缩小时却容易显得拥挤。比较形状间距、外轮廓粗细，以及狼眼和面部周围的留白。如果中心结构不对称，可以简化要求后再生成，不能默认 AI 输出已经适合直接使用。

sections.title: 设计参考不等于可直接使用的模板
sections.body: AI 图像可能存在断线、不一致的对称结构，或不适合肢体曲面的细节。纹身师需要结合具体部位调整线条与布局。照片试戴也只是近似效果，使用前应和原图对照，检查身体形状和光线有没有被一起改变。

prompts.title: 黑灰几何狼头
prompts.text: A front-facing geometric wolf head tattoo, symmetrical angular facets, black and grey shading, clear eyes and muzzle, fine outlines with restrained dotwork, vertical composition, no text, isolated on white.
prompts.note: 这是参考首页案例风格的起点，不保证复现完全相同的设计。

prompts.title: 简洁的几何形状
prompts.text: A small geometric tattoo made of two offset open triangles and a single circle, clean black outlines, consistent line weight, generous empty space, no shading or lettering, isolated on white.
prompts.note: 先用少量形状，再逐步添加细节。

prompts.title: 抽象动物侧面
prompts.text: A geometric fox side-profile tattoo built from a few large angular shapes, clear pointed ears and a long muzzle, black linework with limited grey shading, no border, no text, white background.
prompts.note: 更换动物也会改变轮廓，请保持角度要求一致。

zh.title: 第一次纹身灵感：从个人想法到照片预览
zh.description: 把第一次纹身的想法拆成主题、风格和位置，参考三组提示词与照片检查清单，为和纹身师讨论设计做好准备。
zh.intro: 第一次纹身，可以分开考虑四个问题：想表达什么、喜欢多少细节、考虑哪个位置，以及还有什么需要向纹身师确认。照片预览能帮助你比较外观，但不会替你做决定。

sections.title: 先写一句设计说明
sections.body: 选一个主题，写下为什么喜欢它，再补充轮廓或阴影、紧凑或纵向、安静或醒目等偏好。纹身不一定必须有深刻意义，喜欢图案本身也可以成为起点。把说明与参考图一起保存，方便后面比较不同版本。

sections.title: 比较真正不同的方向
sections.body: 可以针对同一个主题，比较简洁线稿、较粗的剪影和更细致的版本。不要只不断生成几乎一样的图。下面提供植物、风景和几何动物三个方向，你可以用自己喜欢的主体替换，而不是照抄搜索结果。

sections.title: 把位置放进日常场景里考虑
sections.body: 考虑平常穿衣时是否希望纹身可见，以及图案与身体部位的关系。使用目标位置清晰可见、光线均匀的照片。在 Preview 工作室中自由移动、缩放、旋转设计，再生成单张试戴；复用同一设计比较不同位置。照片不能衡量疼痛、预测愈合或保证实际效果。

sections.title: 用预览准备具体的问题
sections.body: 例如：希望的大小能容纳这些细节吗？哪些线条需要简化？这个位置需要改变轮廓吗？把独立设计和身体预览一起给纹身师参考，结合实际技术调整。如果 AI 改动了皮肤、身形或背景，应把设计本身与这些改动分开判断。

sections.title: 了解免费案例与积分规则
sections.body: 首页保存的互动案例可免费浏览。Preview 使用独立测试积分，不扣真实账户余额：生成一张 1K 设计为 1 积分；单张 1K、2K、4K 试戴分别为 1、2、3 积分。上传、保存、复用与自由定位免费。AI 请求仍产生 KIE 测试费用，需明确同意。设计与历史仅存当前浏览器。正式版注册验证邮箱赠送 3 积分的原权益保持不变；Preview 不提供真实购买。

prompts.title: 有个人联系的植物
prompts.text: A small black-ink tattoo of a single rosemary sprig, clean outline, a few clearly separated leaves, no heavy shading, simple vertical composition, no text, isolated on white.
prompts.note: 把迷迭香换成喜欢的植物，第一版只保留一枝。

prompts.title: 安静的风景
prompts.text: A simple tattoo concept of a low sun above one curved ocean wave, black linework, compact balanced composition, open negative space, no lettering or frame, white background.
prompts.note: 再尝试一个较粗轮廓的版本，比较视觉分量。

prompts.title: 有结构的动物图案
prompts.text: A geometric bird tattoo with open wings, a few large angular shapes, recognizable silhouette, black outlines with very limited grey shading, no text, isolated on a white background.
prompts.note: 如果动物结构不一致，先简化要求，并让纹身师检查最终参考。
